en: Sandals with a dainty pair of little wings. Holy power dwells in this armor, and a protective force is at work. Talk to them and the wings seem to flutter in reply... or is that just your imagination?

Platinum slippers. Like gold, platinum resists acid. Being tough and durable, a found pair may be handed down for generations in an adventurer's family. Dig through your closet and you may find Grandpa's or Grandma's Platinum Slippers. Maybe their platinum dentures too.
Pitch-black boots that melt into the darkness. Assassins favor them, so most who own them never die a decent death.
Shoes made of a mysterious glass. You can wear them normally, and they won't break even if you run. Rumor has it that sometimes only one is ever found.

Shoes wrapped in a white radiance. Their holy power reaches even your footsteps; it's said a mere stamp drives off lesser spirits. Priests in this world can serve in the front or back row, but if you put one up front, do give them these.

A cloak worn by many adventurers on their first outing. Don't expect much defense; it serves more to keep out the cold. So even novices can afford it, it has no decoration at all and is priced as low as possible.
A belt martial artists wear as proof of their own training. If your opponent is wearing one, you'd do well to be on your guard.
note: JP calls it a [JP] (waist wrap); 'belt' matches the item name Warrior's Black Belt.

en: A grubby cloak with clasps and buttons coming loose. Your time is finite. Waste it aimlessly and your cloak, too, will soon look like this. And yet the eyes of the fallen have not lost themselves. Why might that be?
This sword is a bit smaller than other two-handed swords. So it allows quicker movement than an ordinary two-handed sword, and lets even adventurers without much strength make powerful attacks.

A cloak that blesses those who find the path they must follow. Its defense is modest, but its spell resistance is strong. Even high-level adventurers are said to find it hard to part with. Some who lose the right to wear it can't bring themselves to toss the cloak that saw them through their youth.
note: Compressed to fit: 'unable to throw it away' folded into 'still keep'.

en: A mantle styled on the new moon. A new-moon night, out of light's reach, is called the 'Holy Darkness', Yaha, when the Kin of Darkness are said to be weakest. Yes, darkness is not always evil. It is a holy chaos that births the power to live, a cradle of the heart that soothes the soul.
note: New term: Yaha ([JP]) = Holy Darkness. Kin of Darkness per glossary.

en: An apron only fully trained servants may wear. The dirtier it gets, the more its wearer is said to have served their master. Each master, and each servant, needs different work done, so the 'Master Apron' comes in many forms.
A cloak with a griffin's wings worked into it. The power of the noble magical beast is said to grant its wearer a courage that flinches before nothing.
note: JP text writes [JP], item name [JP]; both rendered griffin.

en: Great wings of jet black beat only in dreams. Wrap yourself in this mantle and darkness is your ally. Cast off the base light, and welcome to the farthest reaches of the heart.
A mirage is an illusion. This cloak acts on the space around you, making your image appear many times over. Sluggish foes will hardly ever land a hit.

A blade a bit long for a dagger. It comes to a sharp point and has no edge. Some doubt it can kill, given its shape, but assassins favor it. It's easy to carry, and the fatal wounds it deals are hard to notice in an assassination; that seems to be why.
note: JP [JP] (sword) with a dagger-length blade; rendered 'a blade'.

en: "Every adventurer ought to wear this cloth as underwear," say those from the East, but it's rather embarrassing. If you don't mind, wearing one to learn another culture could be fun. Its unique look and feel win some people over.
The bat in the center is iron, but the belt around it is genuine bat leather. Somehow the belt gives off faint ultrasonic waves that protect its owner from confusion.
This is what a fundoshi becomes when worn and its special power is unleashed. Depending on who owned it before, it may come with added value.
A rune born in the process of making magic puppets. By promoting self-repair, it covers the weakness of magic puppets, which have no metabolism.

A belt made of bones of many races, human and elf skulls among them. It is said to be made by demons, for demons. The grudges of those killed for its materials dwell in it. It seems a cruel item, but in truth the demons merely copied what we do.

Only one person in the world may wear this belt: proof of the mightiest fighter. Wear it and you'll be fired up even more. In name there is only one, but you may pick up several on your travels. Yet do not seek value in the belt. Grow strong, so the belt you wear gains value.
note: [JP] read as generic 'fighter' (champion), not the Gladiator class; flag if it should be the class name.

en: Magic paper in everyday use by Kannagi. How it is made is unknown, but it gives off a power to repel evil that is especially strong against evil beings and beings of darkness.
A Magic Seal that amplifies the power of fire. Anyone can equip it easily, but the boost is only modest. If you're a mage, equip at least the next rank up.
A Magic Seal that amplifies the power of ice. Anyone can equip it easily, but the boost is only modest. If you're a mage, equip at least the next rank up.
A Magic Seal that amplifies the power of thunder. Anyone can equip it easily, but the boost is only modest. If you're a mage, equip at least the next rank up.

A dagger of very distinctive shape. You grip it like a fist, the blade jutting forward, so you can slash as naturally as throwing a punch. With one in each hand, you can also cut things aside as you run, or climb a sheer wall by stabbing into it.

Gear devised by the smith Sukebeios, on the idea that a way to attack while defending would be unbeatable. At its debut, many soldiers hailed it as groundbreaking. In practice, only three front-line soldiers could master it, and most were scrapped. Those three are called the Defensive Three.
note: New name: Sukebeios ([JP], pun on sukebe). Compressed to fit.

en: Also known as the 'crescent sword.' Its shape and grip have it called the Jamadhar's successor. Adding throwing to the sword basics of thrust and slash, the Circle Blade truly has no blind spot. But it takes 3 years to learn to catch it cleanly when it comes back.

A huge, supremely lethal machete: a handy one-handed machete simply scaled up. That makes it extremely heavy, and not just anyone can use it. But that very weight is what gives the Scramasax its tremendous destructive power.

Its blade is a mix of glass and iron, 8 to 2. Adding glass to iron lets the blade be bent fairly freely while it's made. With this method, the Silberam's blade is made by twisting one piece of iron into a spiral. The craft is true art. Don't expect much of it as a weapon, though.
note: Ratio kept in source order (glass 8 : iron 2).

en: A wooden box for keeping medicine. Its design came from a land in the East; it is built to stay dry at all times so the medicine inside won't spoil.

The one scale under a dragon's jaw that grows the wrong way is called the 'reverse scale.' Touch it and the dragon flies into a rage and never forgives whoever did. Dragonewts, too, keep a trace of it. It varies by person, but touching it does make them openly annoyed.
A misanga dyed in a savage rabbit's blood. A normal misanga snaps when your wish comes true, but this one grants no wishes and never snaps. Instead, it severs your foe's head from its body.

God, demon, soul, matter. A talisman held by a Kannagi who served, and was loved by, the unknowable power ruling all creation. Ordinary folk can touch it unharmed, but any lowly spirit around would be blown away just by coming near.
A small wooden box engraved with an emblem meaning 'ruler of the world.' Hold it aloft and your foes will tremble in awe and bow down.
A ring set with a pearl. Its pearl is special: a magic-charged pearl said to be a mermaid's gift. Perhaps for that reason, it gives a slight resistance to poison.

A sword from the Eastern lands, once used there to pray for rain. Only a powerful Kannagi could do it, calling rain clouds overhead to bring downpours and lightning on the land. Today few Kannagi have such power, and most of these swords are revered as ornaments.
A ring made of cockatrice bone. Wearing it grants resistance to petrification. In other words, equip it and you can go cockatrice hunting again.
At a glance, an unremarkable wooden ring. Since no one can tell them apart, plain wooden rings sometimes circulate as Sacred Wood Rings. It protects against paralysis.

A ring whose diamond's pure brilliance is said to repel wicked thoughts. It wards off silence, a boon for mages. Now and then one turns up with a diamond tinted red, blue, green or another lovely color. These are rare and sell high, but their magic is weaker.
A ring rusted all over, from who knows what era. Nothing remains of its original form.
A ring only fairies are permitted to wear. It is so tiny that even finding one is hard. Small as it is, it bears decoration, and some fetch very high prices.

A ring set with a gem bearing a pattern like a cat's eye. 'Cat's eye' names a pattern; some stones take it readily, but no stone is called cat's eye. Some Cat's Eye Rings are said to be ultra-rare: gems already magical that went even more cat.
note: [JP] (turned cat) kept as a joke: 'went even more cat'.

en: A ring that slowly restores its wearer's health. Words of thanks to the gods are carved on it; treated with heart, it stands in for a priest's healing spells. Alchemy can do the same, but it uses the laws of the earth; it does not ask the gods for a miracle as priests do.
A ring adorned with a skull. When worn, the skull's eyes begin to glow red. They are said to glow because it is drawing in the wearer's life force.
A ring that gives form to a vow to stay friends forever. This token of friendship across races will show its power for mages and summoners.
An ankh that governs strength. Unleash its hidden power and still greater strength will fill your body.
An ankh that governs wisdom. Unleash its hidden power and still more wisdom will enrich your mind.
note: Item name says Intellect; desc keeps [JP] = wisdom.

en: An ankh that governs faith. Unleash its hidden power, and by the gods' guidance the path you must walk will come into view.
An ankh that governs vitality. Unleash its hidden power and your body will know no fatigue.
An ankh that governs agility. Unleash its hidden power and you will be able to move faster than the eye can see.
An ankh that governs luck. Unleash its hidden power and you will gain luck second to none.

An ointment that has gone along on adventures since long ago, made by blending various herbs in fixed proportions. Every item shop stocks it, and it's reasonably priced. An essential for novice adventurers.
Unlike Salve, this medicine is taken by mouth. It is colorless and clear, with a refreshing sweet-tart taste reminiscent of citrus.

Sprinkle this on, and however deep the sleep, they wake in an instant. It truly wakes anyone, even rousing people who've been up for nights on end, so it once became a health issue. Now it's regulated in many places: adventurers buy it freely, others only once their purpose is checked.

A little antidote herb steeped in water. The herb is addictive: swallowed as-is, it cures poison but brings on 'antidote herb addiction.' People used to hold it in the mouth a while, then spit it out, but young adventurers don't know that trick, so it became a bottled drink.

Herbs that neutralize toxins, steeped in water. The compound is water-soluble. Eaten as-is, they work once digested, but when monsters attack there's no time for that. So adventurers wisely began steeping them beforehand to extract it, and in time the idea became a product.
note: JP says [JP] (detoxifying) herbs even for the paralysis cure; kept. Compressed to fit.

en: A throat-soothing candy. Suck one and your voice comes right back. It works wonders and is so tasty you keep reaching for one when your mouth is bored, so you often find them gone just when you need one! Careful. If you can't resist, have another adventurer carry them.

An herb that calms the confused. Just tear off a leaf and have them smell it, and they'll regain their composure. Beware: make them smell all the leaves at once and they'll go past calm into total apathy.
It cures charm. It's a legitimate medicinal crystal, but who on earth gave it this name? Middle-aged adventurers find it rather awkward to buy.

Water that undoes petrification. It starts as an acid, which alchemy turns into a cure for stone flesh. The body fizzes back to normal, which those who've tried it say feels rather good. Still, asking a mage for a petrify spell plus Stonemelt Water is outright mage harassment. Don't.
A mysterious elixir that can call a soul back into its body. Hold it and you'll find it as warm as skin. Pour it into a dead person's mouth and, unless their soul is lost, they will awaken.

A cure-all for not just headaches but nearly every minor ailment. Made for townsfolk, its effect only lately became known to adventurers. The market sets its price so other drugs won't crash: dear for adventurers who go out and dive into trouble, cheap for townsfolk.

A mass-produced spear. It is actually made of a wood that softens in hot water, so with some skill it can be made portable. But restoring it with hot water takes 2 days, so it is rarely used from its portable state.

Told it would 'be pierced by a Valkyrie with its own Furiwells,' the holy insect Wamrock clung to the spear. A saint then asked for it: "I'm no woman!" Relieved, Wamrock agreed, but the saint was a Valkyrie, neither man nor woman. After much ado, Wamrock was pierced as foretold and writhed in pain, unconvinced.
note: New name: Wamrock ([JP]), [JP] = holy insect; 'it' used, gender unknown. [JP] = Valkyrie (ebt slice_17); JP pun is [JP] containing [JP] 'woman'. Compressed to fit; [JP] = 'after much ado'.

en: Made, of course, for hacking foes apart, but also designed for throwing. Yet one look makes you wonder if anyone really planned for it to be thrown. If you're picking it to throw, don't. There are plenty of other fine throwing weapons.

A hammer made to smash stone and ore. So its head is not mere iron but offcuts of orichalcum, the world's finest material. Offcuts or not, it has orichalcum's hardness and lightness. But mass-made iron ones with no orichalcum reportedly exist, so take care when buying.

A mace said to be modeled on the sun. Legend says its wielder can gain the Sun Spirit's power. Without that legend, though, you'd suspect the 'sun' design was just an excuse to add spikes and make it deadlier.

A deadly weapon: iron balls on a chain, swung round and round. Strong on offense, it leaves your defense weak; against bows and other missiles you may get shot full of holes. Mind your feet when swinging it, too. Step on a nail and, ouch, ouch.

A rare club said to be made of plant roots. Roots sound soft, but some plants grow hard ones: layer them many times over, set them with strong glue, repeat that hundreds of times, and it's done. Hard as any club, yet its grip clings moistly to the hand.

A pair of battledores modeled on the Sun and Moonlight Spirits. A girl who plays with the Moonlight paddle grows up graceful and thoughtful, they say, and a boy with the Sun paddle grows up lively and bold. So nearly every home with kids is said to have a set.

You might call it the ancestor of the bow. Grip the club-like end, set an arrow in its groove and swing with all your might. Only the strong can master it, and it's hard to aim, so hardly anyone uses it now. With enough strength it can outrange a normal bow, but...

Striking for the silver work at its center
and the flame-like ornaments to either side.
Those shot by this bow feel such overwhelming
presence that they fall silent, so it is
surely a masterwork. But who once wielded it
is unknown.
note: Source has explicit 12-char line breaks (10 lines); English kept with breaks at <=46 chars, 6 lines.

en: A flute blessed by the gods. Its clear, light tone lifts the curses of the undead and spirits. Spirits purified by it are said to rise to heaven with very peaceful faces.
As its name says, the sound of its strings relaxes the listener's heart and lures them into a deep sleep. It works even if the listener is a monster.

A trumpet with no fancy tricks, made only to be loud. So loud that even someone too far off to see will hear it clearly. The user, of course, and their allies too, should wear earplugs when it's used if they can.

Bells used in the East to worship or bless the gods. Holding them, Kannagi offer dances to the gods. Their sound also forms a pure-sound barrier, briefly purifying weapons so they can strike spirits normally.
The sound of this lute charms all who hear it. At times, it is said, it steals even the player's heart.

These maracas are enchanted to amplify the rhythm they play, and can make even the quietest ally dance. To monsters, anyone dancing mid-battle is the first to kill. Put the other way, you can draw the enemy's attacks onto a chosen ally.
